messages.subject: Draw additional stuff with grid
parts:
Hello everyone,

I want to draw a circle on top of a ggplot. The circle is of known
diameter measured in the same dimensions as the axes (everything is in
cm).

I don't want to "cheat" with solution such as drawing a open circle
symbol of very large size, or approximating the circle with a
geom_path. So I figure the way to do it is to dive into grid and
modify stuff in the guts of the plot. However I have a problem of
scales:


# produce the base plot
qplot(0,0) + xlim(-5,5) + ylim(-5,5)

# examine the viewport stack
grid.ls(viewport=T)
current.vpTree()
# at that point, I can see that the data point is in panel-3-3
# Q.1: is there any easy/foolproof way to get that programatically?

# naviguate to this view port
current.viewport()
seekViewport("panel-3-3")
current.viewport()
current.vpPath()

# draw stuff
grid.circle(0,0,0.5)
# but these coordinates are relative to the bottom left of the window,
while I want the circule to be drawn relative to the scales of the
current plot. According to chapter 5 of the grid book (p.160), I sould
do:
grid.circle(0,0,0.5, default.units="native")
# but this does not work
# Q. 2: what am I missing here?

# and actually, even though I navigated to "panel-3-3", the
GRID.circle grobs seem to be in a separate tree
grid.ls(viewport=T)

upViewport(0)
current.viewport()
grid.ls(viewport=T)

Thanks in advance for your help.

JiHO

No. I'm hoping this will be easier post layout system rewrite.

> # draw stuff
> grid.circle(0,0,0.5)
> # but these coordinates are relative to the bottom left of the window,
> while I want the circule to be drawn relative to the scales of the

> grid.circle(0,0,0.5, default.units="native")
> # but this does not work
> # Q. 2: what am I missing here?

Unfortunately ggplot2 doesn't use native scales - by the time the data
gets to the panel, it's been converted to npc type values. I did use
native scales previously, but it just ends up being easier to do it
all myself. Unfortunately this results in your problem where you
can't place grid objects relative to the data. I haven't come up with
a good solution to this - in principle you should be able to save the
information used to render the plot and then re-use it for your own
calculations.
